_comment: The recipe's RULES. Every threshold, pattern, and p-value here is your-input: a stated, editable choice, not a record. The pipeline reads records (CSV rows, board responses, BLS rows) and applies these rules to them; the output labels each value accordingly.

ml_ai._soc_hint_note: your-input fallback: O*NET lists AI Engineer and Applied Scientist under 15-1221.00

also_if_title_has_role_word_and_family_w._note: Catches titles like 'Software Engineer, Machine Learning' or 'Software Engineer - AI Platform'. Skipped when the title has a not_if_title_has word (0.2.1: 'Partner Engineer: Partner Intelligence, AI & Apps' and 'AI Automation QA Engineer' were false positives in the first iteration-2 run). Families are checked in file order, so ml_ai (first) wins over software.

data_science._soc_hint_note: your-input fallback only; 'Data Scientists' itself is the O*NET title for 15-2051.00, so most postings match it as a record

data_engineering._soc_hint_note: your-input fallback only. O*NET lists 'Data Engineer' under 15-1242.00 Database Administrators and 'Big Data Engineer' under 15-1243.00 / 15-1243.01, so those titles match as records; the hint is used only when no O*NET title matches

also_if_title_has_role_word_and_family_w._note: 0.4.1: catches 'Software Engineer - Data Platform' / 'Distributed Data Systems' (verify-iteration-1 false negatives). Checked after ml_ai and data_science.

software._soc_hint_note: your-input fallback used only when no O*NET title in the BLS file matches the posting title

_seniority_note: Mid-to-senior persona (about 3.5 years): Senior titles are INCLUDED (author's choice, 0.3.0); staff / principal / lead / manager and above, interns, co-ops and PhD-titled roles are excluded. A Senior posting that asks 5+ years is still ruled out by description_rules.years_of_experience (persona 3.5 + tolerance 1).
_changelog: 0.1.1 (2026-10-02): added \bph.?d\b after the first live pass put two 'Systems PhD - Software Engineer' postings on an MS student's Apply list (evidence/05-first-live-smoke).

0.2.0 (2026-10-02): author re-scoped to mid-level AI Engineer roles on the Microsoft AI stack. ml_ai family first and widened (composite role-word + AI-word titles); seniority rules re-cut for ~3.5 years; added description_rules (TODO 7, from the G3 finding that both AI Engineer rows were disqualified only in their job descriptions) and microsoft_ai_stack_terms.

0.2.1 (2026-10-02): composite AI-title rule ignores partner/sales/solutions/support/QA/test titles; 'can't sponsor' statements are now counted on every posting of a found board and shown per company. They are NOT used to drop a company: a first draft of 0.2.1 dropped any company with one such posting from the networking list, but the live run showed the statements are role-specific ('for this role, at this time'). Verkada: 156 of 307 postings, mostly sales/ops, not its backend roles. Twin Health: 23 of 39, but not 'Senior AI Engineer'. So that draft rule was withdrawn before commit. Evidence: evidence/24-*.

0.3.0 (2026-10-02): author asked to include Senior titles and Data Engineer / Data Scientist roles. Removed the two Senior patterns; added data_science and data_engineering families (with O*NET-backed SOC lookups); added Microsoft data-stack terms. Code unchanged (75f3c41).

0.4.0 (2026-10-03): years rule v2 (largest required line; or-alternatives; preferred lines never decide; list items never headings) and fit divided by the scheme maximum (12) instead of 8. Evidence: 16 live descriptions read on 2026-10-03 (verify-iteration files).

0.4.1 (2026-10-03): from verify-iteration-1 — (1) years are judged per sentence, so 'a plus' in the next sentence no longer makes a requirement optional (Twin Health 'Senior AI Engineer', 5+ years, was wrongly kept); (2) family words added for false negatives found in the boundary scan: AI (reinforcement learning, model serving, model inference, foundation model) and data engineering (data platform, distributed data, data infrastructure/pipelines/systems, big data, data warehouse, lakehouse, ETL, business intelligence engineer); (3) the verification sample's boundary titles rotate across companies.

0.4.2 (2026-10-03): from verify-iteration-2 — 'preferred' after a years number (and before any 'required') marks that mention preferred ('2+ years industry experience strongly preferred'); 'N+ years of expertise' and 'expertise (N+ years)' count like experience. Apptronik 'Senior Reinforcement Learning Engineer' (requires expertise (5+ years)) was wrongly kept at 2+.

us_location._note: A posting is kept when ANY part of its location string names the US by one of these terms. A bare 'Remote' with no country is kept but flagged 'remote, country unstated' for the human gate.

_sponsorship_note: same_family = the company's sponsored job titles (80 Days CSV, record) include a title from the SAME family as the posting. Tiers are checked top to bottom; first match wins. Likely/Possible are soft tiers in role-scorer.mjs and demote Apply to Consider.

fit._note: fit p = min(1, scheme score / scheme max). The max is computed from scheme.json (title 3 + 8 skills × 1 + any-skill 0.5 + degree 0.5 = 12), so 1.0 means a complete match rather than '8 points or more' (0.3.x divided by 8 and saturated for skill-rich résumés).

timeline._note: available_days = (opt_start_date - today) + unemployment_days_allowed; margin = available_days - hiring_lag_days; factor = 1.0 if margin >= full_margin_days, margin / full_margin_days if 0 < margin < full_margin_days, 0.0 (gate closed) if margin <= 0.

network._note: A company goes on the networking list only when its board WAS found and fetched, zero postings passed the family + US + seniority filters, and its company-level sponsorship tier is one of these.

discovery._note: Slugs are guessed from the CSV company name and website. Lever, Workday, iCIMS and SmartRecruiters are not probed ([TODO: DEV] in the recipe).

_title_families_note: Families are checked in this order (ml_ai first, so 'Data Scientist, Machine Learning' is ml_ai). Which families are TARGETED is the persona's choice (target_families); families not targeted are still recognised and counted as 'other family'.

description_rules._note: Read the posting DESCRIPTION, not just the title. Each phrase is matched case-insensitively against the posting text (record); the choice of phrases is your-input. A match rules the posting out before scoring and the report lists it with the matched phrase.

years_of_experience._note: Years rule v2 (0.4.0): the description is split into lines and section headings (preferred vs required; list items are never headings; a line saying 'a plus', 'nice to have' or 'bonus' is preferred); each 'N+ years … experience' line counts its largest number, or its smallest when the mentions are joined by 'or'; the requirement is the largest required line, and preferred lines never decide. The posting is ruled out when that requirement is greater than persona experience_years + tolerance_years. No years stated means kept.

description_rules._company_wide_note: no_sponsorship_phrases are ALSO counted on every posting of a found board, whatever its family, and the report shows 'N of M postings say they can't sponsor that role' per company. The statements are role-specific, so they rule out the posting that carries them, never the whole company.

_stack_note: Microsoft AI and data stack terms, reported per posting (record text match). Not a vote and not a filter.
